stage: the runtime source hash, the half of the fingerprint that needs no decision
what_codex_asked: a fresh fingerprint of the selected world's authored dependencies, without the generated compiled pack, because a change DURING a compile slips past a guard that only compares CompileInputHash
what_was_missing: CompileInputHash covers what the COMPILER reads - the campaign manifest, its module files, the schemas and the photoBook authoring specs - and NOT the runtime content outside the module folders: game/content/world world plots, cutscenes timelines, the animation catalogue and the studio recipes. There are twenty-one such authored files today
what_this_adds: PlayPreparation.RuntimeSourceHash(root): a SEPARATE value, so a caller can compare both and know what each covers. It hashes the authored runtime files and, like CompileInputHash, EXCLUDES every *.compiled.v1.json - the compiler writes those itself, so hashing them would make a legitimate compile look like an authored change
verified_behaviour: a change to a world plot CHANGES the hash (the change that used to slip past), writing a compiled pack does NOT change it, the value is stable, and it differs from CompileInputHash
the_boundary_and_its_cost: it covers ALL authored runtime content, not only the selected campaign's, so a change to ANOTHER campaign's world plot also invalidates a run. That direction is chosen on purpose - a false-stale wastes a compile while a missed change launches a scene the author did not ask for - and narrowing it needs a mapping from a selection to its runtime FILES, which the manifest does not carry today: it names scene IDS, not paths. The scope question (a)/(b) is still Codex's to answer, and the call site is his
